final_answer: The Roman Empire fell due to a complex interplay of factors. Political instability, economic decline, military overextension, and external invasions all contributed. Political fragmentation and frequent leadership changes weakened governance. Economic troubles arose from heavy taxation, inflation, and reliance on slave labor. Military strain came from defending vast borders and recruiting loyal troops. External pressures from Germanic tribes and the Huns accelerated collapse. While no single cause dominated, internal decay likely made the Empire vulnerable to external threats.
